items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: My favorite composer is Sergei Rachmaninoff. You know. And then I’m crazy about Debussy and Ravel and Satie, and those people who write — Chopin — all those people who write beautiful, beautiful melodies. They are my heroes you know.

ctx.x: Did you start with the second movement?

Yes I wrote a piece and then I recorded it here at home you know and she said, “Wow, that sounds like a second movement of a concerto. Okay. You know what you have to do, I don’t have to tell you again.” The second one is more simple to be honest. It’s more melodic. It’s not very technical and it’s not very complicated at all. Because to be honest, I’m not a big fan of those kind of trumpet concertos, the modern music that has no melodies [scats]. I say wow, I cannot repeat that in my dreams, or I cannot memorize…

I would totally agree and it was so melodic, the third movement of this second concerto, that I pulled out some staff paper and I decided to do what I fifty some years ago had to © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
